term.def: The network of chips, cloud services, data and software that come together to build and run AI systems, from raw materials to finished product.

prompt.prompt: List three risks if [a key AI tool or vendor] we rely on became unavailable overnight, and suggest two backup options for each risk.

quiz.q: Bloomberg reports that India is emerging as an AI haven seeking a boost from new US chip curbs.
quiz.why: This is what the Bloomberg headline states directly.

quiz.q: News On AIR reports that India, the US and eight other nations signed a declaration to safeguard AI supply chains.
quiz.why: This matches the News On AIR headline exactly.

quiz.q: AI systems genuinely understand meaning the way a human mind does.
quiz.why: AI finds patterns in data and predicts likely outputs, it does not understand in the human sense.

quiz.q: You must know how to code to use most AI tools at work today.
quiz.why: Most modern AI tools are built for plain language instructions, no coding needed.

quiz.q: AI tools can sound confident while giving an answer that is completely wrong.
quiz.why: AI models predict likely words, so fluent and wrong answers can look identical to fluent and right ones.
